ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graph of the function $y=2x+b$ intersects with the graph of the function $y=kx-3$ at point $P$. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx-3>2x+b$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Observing the graph, we find: when $x<4$, the graph of the function $y=2x+b$ is below the graph of the function $y=kx-3$, \\
$\therefore$ the solution set of the inequality $kx-3>2x+b$ is $\boxed{x<4}$.

The straight line labeled y=kx-3 is a decreasing straight line slanting downward to the right, and the straight line labeled y=2x+b is an increasing straight line slanting upward to the right. Then reason: The inequality kx-3>2x+b means that the function value of the straight line y=kx-3 is greater than the function value of the straight line y=2x+b, that is, on the graph, the x range where y=kx-3 is above y=2x+b. Therefore the solution set corresponding to strictly greater than is x<4.
